newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares trade quietly after summit.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares trade quietly after summit.

text.p: Trading on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange opened quietly on Thursday morning, as the market took a wait-and-see attitude to Israeli-Palestinian negotiations, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares was off 0.44 percent or 0.82 points at 183.59 in the first rounds of trading. The Maof 25 index was down 0.45 at 193.14.
Trading was also quiet due to the holiday of Succoth, which runs all this week, said Eyal Kolka of Sigma Securities. The stock exchange closes early and many traders are on holiday.

"There isn't any good news yet," said Kolka, referring to the results of a two-day summit that wound up on Wednesday in Washington. The participants failed to resolve any of the issues that caused clashes between Israeli soldiers and Palestinians since last week and has killed 73 people.

However, the two sides agreed to intensify talks starting on Sunday with mediation efforts by U.S. peace coordinator Dennis Ross. The market will wait and see the results of those talks," Kolka said. In the meantime, "the uncertainty will continue".
Among Mishtanim shares, the only one to show much movement was Nice Systems, which was down 4.5 percent in early trading. Nice's Nasdaq share price fell sharply on Wednesday.
